7bb382e41e03376a: Queues: a queue manages tasks submitted by the developer. GCD queues always handle tasks in first-in, first-out order, but tasks take different amounts of time, so the first task handled need not finish first. Queues can be serial or concurrent. A serial queue processes one task at a time and starts the next only after the previous task finishes. A concurrent queue can process multiple tasks simultaneously. An underlying thread pool executes the submitted tasks managed by the queue. A serial queue needs only one thread in its underlying pool; a concurrent queue is the opposite.

Every screen has a refresh rate: the recommended iphone rate is 60Hz, meaning the GPU refreshes the screen 60 times per second, with 16.67ms between refreshes. The screen contents remain unchanged during that interval, called a frame. fps means frames per second: how many frames appear each second. Refresh rate matters little for static content, but during animation or scrolling, fps directly reflects smoothness.

90c0a5839902b6d7: First, understand pixels. Each point on the screen is a pixel composed of R, G, and B values, sometimes with alpha. When several layers cover an area, they jointly affect its final appearance. For example, a blue upper layer (RGB=0,0,1) at 50% opacity over a red lower layer (RGB=1,0,0) produces purple (RGB=0.5,0,0.5). This blending consumes GPU resources, particularly when more than two layers are involved. If only the upper blue layer needs to be visible, set its opacity to 100%. The GPU can then ignore the layers below and avoid unnecessary calculations.
